lines.text: Four half circles inside a square make a pretty flower. How much of it is shaded?
lines.caption: Four half circles inside a square make a pretty flower. How much of it is shaded?

lines.text: Many kids find the white petals and stop there. <short pause> But that's NOT what we're asked!
lines.caption: Many kids find the white petals and stop there. But that's NOT what we're asked!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the shaded part together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the shaded part together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A square has side four. A half circle is drawn inside the square on each side.
lines.caption: A square has side four. A half circle is drawn inside the square on each side.

lines.text: The half circles overlap in four white petals. What is the total shaded area?
lines.caption: The half circles overlap in four white petals. What is the total shaded area?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what are we really looking for?
lines.caption: So what are we really looking for?

lines.text: Each half circle sits on one side of the square. That side is its diameter.
lines.caption: Each half circle sits on one side of the square. That side is its diameter.

lines.text: So every half circle has a radius of two.
lines.caption: So every half circle has a radius of two.

lines.text: A white petal is where two half circles overlap.
lines.caption: A white petal is where two half circles overlap.

lines.text: We want the colored part. That's the square, minus all four petals.
lines.caption: We want the colored part. That's the square, minus all four petals.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's our plan: find the area of one petal first.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's our plan: find the area of one petal first.

lines.text: Cut the big square into four small squares, each two by two.
lines.caption: Cut the big square into four small squares, each two by two.

lines.text: Each small square holds exactly one petal, from its corner to the center.
lines.caption: Each small square holds exactly one petal, from its corner to the center.

lines.text: Let's zoom in on the bottom left one.
lines.caption: Let's zoom in on the bottom left one.

lines.text: Only two half circles come into this small square. Each one makes a quarter circle.
lines.caption: Only two half circles come into this small square. Each one makes a quarter circle.

lines.text: Their overlap is the petal. Now draw the diagonal. It cuts the petal into two equal slices.
lines.caption: Their overlap is the petal. Now draw the diagonal. It cuts the petal into two equal slices.

lines.text: Take the blue quarter circle, and remove the triangle under the diagonal.
lines.caption: Take the blue quarter circle, and remove the triangle under the diagonal.

lines.text: What's left is exactly one slice.
lines.caption: What's left is exactly one slice.

lines.text: The quarter circle has radius two. Two squared is four, and a quarter of four pi is just pi!
lines.caption: The quarter circle has radius two. Two squared is four, and a quarter of four pi is just pi!

lines.text: The triangle has two legs of length two, so its area is two.
lines.caption: The triangle has two legs of length two, so its area is two.

lines.text: So one slice is pi minus two.
lines.caption: So one slice is pi minus two.

lines.text: A petal is two slices, so one petal is two pi minus four.
lines.caption: A petal is two slices, so one petal is two pi minus four.

lines.text: All four petals are the same shape and size.
lines.caption: All four petals are the same shape and size.

lines.text: So four petals make eight pi minus sixteen.
lines.caption: So four petals make eight pi minus sixteen.

lines.text: The shaded part is the square, sixteen, minus all the petals.
lines.caption: The shaded part is the square, sixteen, minus all the petals.

lines.text: Open the bracket. Sixteen minus eight pi plus sixteen makes thirty-two minus eight pi.
lines.caption: Open the bracket. Sixteen minus eight pi plus sixteen makes thirty-two minus eight pi.

lines.text: That's about forty-three percent of the square, a bit less than half. That looks right!
lines.caption: That's about forty-three percent of the square, a bit less than half. That looks right!

lines.text: The answer is B, thirty-two minus eight pi!
lines.caption: The answer is B, thirty-two minus eight pi!

lines.text: Here's a faster way. Let's add up all four half circles.
lines.caption: Here's a faster way. Let's add up all four half circles.

lines.text: Each one has radius two. Two squared is four, and half of four pi is two pi.
lines.caption: Each one has radius two. Two squared is four, and half of four pi is two pi.

lines.text: Together, all four half circles make eight pi. But the square is only sixteen!
lines.caption: Together, all four half circles make eight pi. But the square is only sixteen!

lines.text: Together they cover the square with no gaps. The shaded parts are covered once.
lines.caption: Together they cover the square with no gaps. The shaded parts are covered once.

lines.text: Each petal sits inside two half circles, so it was counted twice.
lines.caption: Each petal sits inside two half circles, so it was counted twice.

lines.text: No spot is inside three of them. Only the center point touches all four.
lines.caption: No spot is inside three of them. Only the center point touches all four.

lines.text: That means eight pi is the square, plus each petal one extra time.
lines.caption: That means eight pi is the square, plus each petal one extra time.

lines.text: The petals are eight pi minus sixteen. Then the shaded part is thirty-two minus eight pi again.
lines.caption: The petals are eight pi minus sixteen. Then the shaded part is thirty-two minus eight pi again.

lines.text: Use this trick whenever overlapping shapes cover a whole region.
lines.caption: Use this trick whenever overlapping shapes cover a whole region.

lines.text: C, eight pi minus sixteen, is the white petals. A great step, but not the shaded part!
lines.caption: C, eight pi minus sixteen, is the white petals. A great step, but not the shaded part!

lines.text: D, sixteen minus two pi, takes away only one half circle.
lines.caption: D, sixteen minus two pi, takes away only one half circle.

lines.text: A, sixteen minus four pi, takes away only two half circles, like one whole circle.
lines.caption: A, sixteen minus four pi, takes away only two half circles, like one whole circle.

lines.text: E, forty-eight minus eight pi, is about twenty-three. That's bigger than the whole square!
lines.caption: E, forty-eight minus eight pi, is about twenty-three. That's bigger than the whole square!

lines.text: Quick check: the shaded part plus the petals must make sixteen. And it does!
lines.caption: Quick check: the shaded part plus the petals must make sixteen. And it does!

lines.text: Your turn! This time the square has side six.
lines.caption: Your turn! This time the square has side six.

lines.text: The same four half circles are drawn inside. What is the shaded area now?
lines.caption: The same four half circles are drawn inside. What is the shaded area now?

lines.text: Hint: find the radius first!
lines.caption: Hint: find the radius first!

lines.text: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Let's check. The side is six, so the radius is three.
lines.caption: Let's check. The side is six, so the radius is three.

lines.text: Pi times three squared is nine pi. So each half circle is half of nine pi.
lines.caption: Pi times three squared is nine pi. So each half circle is half of nine pi.

lines.text: All four together make eighteen pi.
lines.caption: All four together make eighteen pi.

lines.text: The square is thirty-six, so the petals are eighteen pi minus thirty-six.
lines.caption: The square is thirty-six, so the petals are eighteen pi minus thirty-six.

lines.text: The shaded part is thirty-six minus the petals. That's seventy-two minus eighteen pi!
lines.caption: The shaded part is thirty-six minus the petals. That's seventy-two minus eighteen pi!

lines.text: If you got that, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you got that, amazing work!

lines.text: When two shapes overlap, adding up their areas counts the overlap twice.
lines.caption: When two shapes overlap, adding up their areas counts the overlap twice.

lines.text: So the overlap is the shapes added up, minus the area they cover.
lines.caption: So the overlap is the shapes added up, minus the area they cover.
